title: The Last Voyage of the Black Vesper (Solo)
text: A single-protagonist narrative escape from the brig of the pirate brig Black Vesper. The year is 1721. The protagonist is Mira 'Ironhand' Castellanos, Quartermaster of the Vesper. Captain Mordecai Vane has betrayed the crew, drugged the rum, and locked everyone in the brig. The other senior crew lie unconscious around Mira in the cell — she is the only one awake. The ship is sailing toward Port Royal where the British Navy waits to hang them all. She must escape alone, retake the ship, find the ledger that proves Vane's betrayal, and change course before 06:00.

title: Mira 'Ironhand' Castellanos
text: Quartermaster of the Black Vesper. Second-in-command, the one who kept the ledgers and read men's faces. Vane was her captain and her only friend for seven years. She has a sharp eye for the true value or purpose of any object she examines (Appraise). Her starting possessions: a worn ledger fragment with cipher entries she does not yet recognise, and a small folding knife sharp enough to cut rope but too small to force a lock.

title: Win Conditions
text: Best ending requires: (1) escape the brig, (2) navigate the lower decks without raising the alarm, (3) neutralise the loyalists on the upper deck, (4) recover the ledger from the Captain's Cabin, (5) change course at the helm before 06:00, and (6) confront Vane with the correct evidence to take him alive.

title: Narrative tone
text: Tense, conspiratorial, period-appropriate to 1721 Caribbean piracy. No magic. Every puzzle has a physical, chemical, or navigational explanation. The Game Master narrates in second person ('You see...', 'You hear...'). Mira speaks in first person when she chooses to.

title: Cell door cannot be forced
text: The cell door is reinforced with naval-grade fittings, hinges bolted from the outside. Forcing it is impossible and will only generate noise that raises the alarm meter.

title: Loud noises wake the jailor
text: Crooked Hal is drunk but light-sleeping. Any loud action in the brig (shouting, banging on bars, dropping heavy items) wakes him. A waking Hal means an alarm and almost certain failure of Act 1.

title: Item combination is core
text: Mira is a pirate. She has spent her career making do with inadequate tools. Any two inventory items can be combined if it makes physical sense (rope + knife → cut strip, herbs + hot water → infusion, vial + flame → heated container).

title: The Brig
text: A damp iron cell in the belly of the Black Vesper. Salt-crusted walls. A swinging oil lantern on a chain hangs from the ceiling, lit but dim. A small porthole shows the moon and stars — too small to crawl through. The cell occupies the left half of the room; a heavy iron door with a naval-grade padlock is the only exit. Across the room, beyond arm's reach through the bars, sits Crooked Hal at a wooden desk, slumped, snoring, with a mug at his elbow and a keyring at his belt. The three other senior crew lie unconscious on the cell floor — drugged, breathing, but useless. A ceiling hook is bolted into the timber directly above Hal's desk.

title: The Lower Decks
text: Three rooms: the Cargo Hold (crates with weight markings, a balance scale on the wall), the Galley (Vane's recent meal, an open captain's log written in a cipher, a locked spice cabinet), and the Powder Room (a locked chest of gunpowder cartridges with a brass key inside, a four-dial combination, a child's embroidery on the wall as the clue).

title: The Upper Deck
text: Open air, stars overhead. The ship's wheel is manned by a loyalist named Garrett. Two more loyalists patrol the deck. Three stations: the Mast (a flare pistol in the crow's nest, reached by a rigging puzzle), the Bell (rung in a specific sequence to summon loyalists for ambush), and the Constellation Sphere (a celestial pedestal that aligns to draw a key shape for the Captain's Cabin).

title: The Captain's Cabin
text: Reinforced mahogany door opened only by the constellation key. Inside: a desk piled with charts, a wall of books (sequence puzzle), a tilting portrait hiding a wall safe (five-symbol lock), a rotating globe with a hidden chamber (folded Royal Navy pardon offer), and a locked sea-chest with a three-ship-name dial lock containing the ledger and a brass kraken key.

title: The Helm
text: Dawn breaking. Port Royal coastline visible. The wheel is locked by a brass kraken mechanism (kraken key fits) and bound by ropes that must be cut in the correct order. The wheel itself is a three-dial mechanism for plotting course — three corrections required, drawn from earlier acts. Vane will emerge belowdecks for the final confrontation, resolved by presenting the correct evidence.

title: Worn Ledger Fragment
text: Partial records of crew expenses and shares. Some entries are in a cipher Mira does not yet recognise. Reveals more under Appraise: the cipher uses a simple letter shift. Crew tattoo symbols are noted in the margins (relevant to Act 4's wall safe).

title: Small Folding Knife
text: A pocket folding knife with a two-inch blade. Sharp enough to cut rope, leather, cloth, or skin. Too small to force a lock or pry a hinge. Quiet to use.

title: Oil Lantern
text: Wrought iron, hung on a chain from the ceiling above the centre of the room. Lit, dim flame. The candle stub inside cannot be removed without snuffing it — but the flame itself can heat objects held close to it. The chain is within reach if Mira stands on the bunk.

title: Wooden Bunk
text: A narrow plank bed bolted to the cell wall. Sturdy enough to stand on. The straw mattress contains nothing of note, but the underside of the plank has a single rusted nail driven partway in — long enough to be worked free with the knife if Mira is patient (quiet action).

title: Rusted Bent Nail
text: Once worked free, the nail is about three inches long with a slight bend. Too short to pick the cell padlock on its own, but combined with a sturdy length of wire or a thin metal strip it becomes a workable pick. Mira's Appraise: 'Half a lockpick. Find the other half.'

title: Coil of Rope
text: Twenty feet of hemp rope coiled in the dark corner of the cell — left behind by the bo'sun before he was drugged. Strong, dry. Useful for swinging, tying, lowering objects through bars, or as a sling.

title: Surgeon's Herb Packet
text: Found in Dr. Whitcombe's coat pocket on the cell floor. Three varieties of dried herbs labelled in Eliza's careful hand: 'valerian', 'hops', 'passionflower'. Eliza's recipe book (also in her pocket) notes: 'Brewed together in hot water — a sleeping draught strong enough to drop a horse. Effect in five minutes.'

title: Surgeon's Leather Recipe Book
text: Eliza's journal. The relevant page describes the three-herb sleeping draught: requires hot water, steeped for two minutes. Other recipes (poisons, antidotes, smoke agent, invisible ink reveal) hint at Act 2 and beyond but are not usable in the brig.

title: Empty Glass Vial
text: Eliza's heatproof vial. Stoppered with cork. Capacity about one shot of liquid. Can be held close to the lantern flame to heat its contents.

title: Cracked Brass Compass
text: Jin's compass. The needle is unreliable now but the back-plate is unusually thick polished brass — concave on one side. Mira's Appraise: 'Polished brass, slightly concave. Will focus a flame the way a burning glass focuses sunlight.' Useful for concentrating the lantern's heat onto a small target.

title: Jailor's Keyring
text: A heavy iron ring with four keys, hanging from a leather loop on Crooked Hal's belt. One of the keys matches the cell padlock. The keyring is out of arm's reach through the cell bars — Hal sits at his desk roughly eight feet from the bars.

title: Hal's Tin Mug
text: A dented tin mug half-full of dark rum, sitting on Hal's desk within reach of his right hand. He drinks from it absent-mindedly every few minutes, even in sleep. Anything dropped into the mug from above will be consumed.

title: Iron Ceiling Hook
text: A heavy iron hook bolted into a roof beam, positioned almost directly above Hal's desk. Likely used historically to hang lanterns or pulleys. A rope thrown and snagged over the hook can be used to lower a small object directly onto the desk — or onto the mug — from a swing-arc that originates inside the cell bars.

title: Crooked Hal
text: The jailor. Mid-fifties, lean, sun-leathered, two missing fingers on his left hand. Drunk and asleep at his desk, snoring loudly. His drinking has been a problem for years. He wakes at any sharp noise but sleeps deeply through the rhythmic creaks of the ship. He carries the cell keys on his belt and drinks from a tin mug of rum on the desk. State: asleep_drunk. If he wakes, the alarm meter spikes and Act 1 fails.

title: Unconscious Crewmates
text: Jin, Tomás, Eliza, and Kwame — drugged by the rum Vane dosed before the raid. Breathing, stable, but will not wake until well past dawn. Their pockets and packs are searchable: Eliza carries her vial, herbs, and recipe book; Jin carries her compass and star chart; Tomás's flint and steel are in his belt pouch; Kwame's rope is already on the cell floor beside him. Their lives depend on Mira.

title: Open the cell padlock
objective: Open the cell door without waking Hal.
text: The cell padlock is naval-grade and cannot be forced. There are two viable approaches: (A) retrieve Hal's keyring, which requires neutralising him first without noise (see puzzle.sedate_hal); (B) construct a lockpick from the bent nail combined with a thin metal strip — but the strip must come from outside the cell, so this path also requires getting an arm or hook to Hal's desk first. Path A is faster and the intended solution.

title: Sedate Crooked Hal
objective: Get Hal into a sleep deep enough that his keyring can be safely lifted.
text: Hal drinks from his mug at intervals even in his sleep. Drop a strong sedative into the mug and within five minutes he will be unrousable. The sedative: brew Eliza's three herbs (valerian, hops, passionflower) in hot water inside the glass vial. The vial must be heated — the lantern flame focused through Jin's concave brass compass-back can heat the vial enough to steep the herbs in two minutes. Once brewed, the draught must be delivered to the mug from inside the cell — accomplished by throwing rope over the ceiling hook above Hal's desk, then using the rope and folding knife to lower the stoppered vial across the gap, uncorking it remotely (a slip-knot mechanism), and letting the draught fall into the mug. Any noise during this process risks waking Hal.

title: Retrieve the keyring
objective: Get the keyring from Hal's belt into the cell.
text: Once Hal is deeply sedated (post-puzzle.sedate_hal), Mira can use the rope-over-hook rig with the folding knife tied to the end as a grappling weight to hook the keyring's leather loop and lift it free. Requires steady hands; the unconscious crew on the floor cannot help. Successful retrieval yields item.hal_keyring.

title: Exit the brig
objective: Unlock the cell and ascend to the lower decks.
text: With the keyring in hand, the cell padlock opens silently. The stairwell to the lower decks is at the far end of Hal's room. Climbing it triggers Act 2 — footsteps and Vane's voice can be heard above. The alarm meter begins for Act 2. Mira may choose to drag the unconscious crew to a hidden corner (slows time but preserves their safety) or leave them — narrative consequence either way.

title: Escape the Brig
text: Open the cell door and reach the stairwell. The intended sequence: (1) find the rope coil and recover items from unconscious crew, (2) work the bent nail free from the bunk as backup, (3) brew the sleeping draught in the heated vial, (4) deliver the draught to Hal's mug via the ceiling-hook rope rig, (5) wait for him to drink and fall deep, (6) hook the keyring with the rope-and-knife grapple, (7) unlock the cell, (8) ascend.

title: Navigate the Lower Decks
text: Pass through cargo hold (balance scale weighted to door's counterweight), galley (decode captain's log via Caesar cipher shift 3, brew tainted rum for the watch crew's ration barrel), and powder room (four-dial chest combination from embroidered date in ledger). Outcome: stairwell to upper deck opens; tainted rum optionally pre-empts loyalist resistance.

title: Neutralise the Loyalists
text: Three stations: climb rigging to crow's nest (knot sequence: bowline, clove hitch, sheet bend), ring bell in signal (three then two) to cluster loyalists for non-lethal ambush, align constellation sphere to draw cabin-key shape. Decide: tie Garrett (safer, slower) or knock out (faster, risk of waking).

title: Recover the Ledger
text: Inside the Captain's Cabin: open the book wall (shanty verse sequence — missing words on captain's hat and teacup bottom), tilt the portrait to reveal wall safe (five crew tattoo symbols from ledger margins), align globe to Port Royal for the Navy pardon letter, open sea-chest (three ship-name dials from log + safe + sphere). Acquire ledger and kraken key.

title: Change Course
text: Cut wheel-binding ropes in correct order (rope-tension puzzle), insert kraken key, plot three-dial course correction from prior-act clues. Final confrontation with Vane resolved by presenting correct evidence — ledger for greed, pardon letter for treason, log for the brother. Correct trio: take Vane alive.

title: What about Jin's compass?
text: When Mira examines the compass on Jin's belt, Appraise reveals the back-plate is unusually thick concave brass — useful for focusing light or heat.

title: Heat without removing the candle
text: The lantern's flame cannot be safely moved, but objects can be held close to it. A reflector — say, a polished concave brass surface — would concentrate the heat onto a small target like a stoppered vial.

title: Reach across the gap
text: The cell bars stop arms, not rope. The ceiling hook above Hal's desk is the bridge. With the rope thrown over it from inside the cell, Mira can lower or hoist small objects to and from the desk.

title: Why brew it at all?
text: Hal drinks from his mug even in sleep. The mug is the only reliable delivery system. The draught must be liquid, the mug must already contain rum to mask it, and the rope-hook rig is the only way to reach the mug from inside the cell.
